visualReview.notes: Inspected the raised four-front outline, triangular works, two timber crossings, town blocks and full stone mole geometry against the original Copernicus cape surface.

sharedSurfaceReview.notes: Verified dated World Explorer placement and bound earth, gravel, stone, timber siding and roof materials. The geographic flat-plane check clips low harbor portions below the cape datum. The native elevation view shows the complete harbor geometry. Viewer unloading passed.

mediumFiReview.notes: All four levels preserve the fort and harbor plan, including the four ravelins, two interior earthworks and both bridge spans. Higher levels add timber piers, railings, palisade, gables and doorways.

terrain.source: Copernicus DEM GLO-30 © DLR e.V. and Airbus Defence and Space GmbH

geographicReview.notes: The December 1704 measured plan, historic compass and scale establish the relative plan. Petrovskaya 15 constrains the third bastion. Model elevations use the independent Copernicus GLO-30 crop. Present-day reclamation and the original coastline limit alignment accuracy. Confirmed that the placement is eligible at the modeled date and withheld for undated and later viewing.

fidelityReview.scope: Troitskoy, the early Taganrog Fortress and its stone harbor moles, as surveyed in December 1704. The model covers the cape-top earthwork, ravelins, four landward fronts, two timber bridges and the near harbor.
fidelityReview.notes: The two archive reproductions record the earthwork profile, four landward fronts, the adjacent harbor and the town blocks. Roof details, bridge elevations, historical drainage and the mole tops over reclaimed areas are approximate.

imageryReview.notes: Inspected the exact public-domain Lyall print already published by Qualla first. The signed 1704 survey controls the model. The 1825 print provides an independent view of the later cape and harbor.

validation.sharedCaptureScope: The early fortress and harbor as surveyed in December 1704, displayed for 1705.

limitations: The representation centers on the December 1704 archival survey. Display dates cover the following year as an approximate appearance interval.

The absolute historical outline and elevations are approximate. Fit uses a known landward bastion site, the historic compass and Rute scale. Present-day port reclamation, roads and surviving cut slopes change the terrain around the cape.

The dry ditch is a shallow channel between modelled banks resting on independently sampled modern terrain. Harbor moles remain visible above the existing surface through reclaimed areas, where their present surface height is an estimate.

Townspeople’s buildings, gates, timber work and roof details are restrained reconstructions. The 1704 plan documents street blocks and some raised structures. The individual roof forms are estimates, and the church and permanent fort facilities that opened in later years are outside this appearance.
